member.name: M:RomValidator.Pages.ValidatePage.LooksLikeBinaryContent(System.String)
member.summary: Heuristically determines whether the file preview is binary rather than text, by checking for a high proportion of NUL / non-printable control characters and non-ASCII bytes. Compressed/binary DAT files (e.g. RetroAchievements.dat) contain many bytes >= 0x80 that are not control characters, so both are counted. Used to avoid reporting binary files as XML parsing bugs.

member.name: M:RomValidator.Pages.ValidatePage.LooksLikeXmlContent(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether the file preview looks like XML text at all. Valid XML must start with '<' after an optional BOM and whitespace (e.g. "<?xml", "<datafile", "<!--"). Anything else (e.g. an emulator's playhistory.dat) cannot be a valid DAT file, so it is a user-input mistake rather than an application bug and must not trigger a bug report.

member.name: M:RomValidator.Pages.ValidatePage.HasXmlTextBom(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether the preview starts with a UTF-16 or UTF-32 byte order mark. Valid XML may be encoded as UTF-16/UTF-32; because the preview is decoded as Latin-1 those files look binary, so the BOM must be trusted and the content validated by the XML reader instead of the binary heuristics.
member.param: The raw DAT file preview.
member.returns: True when the preview starts with a UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM.

member.name: M:RomValidator.Services.HashCalculator.MyRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
\\.(zip|7z|rar)$
Options:
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.ExplicitCapture
Explanation:
○ Match '.'.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Zz].
○ Match a character in the set [Ii\u0130].
○ Match a character in the set [Pp].
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '7'.
○ Match a character in the set [Zz].
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Rr].
○ Match a character in the set [Aa].
○ Match a character in the set [Rr].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
